channel.title: Pogue Digital Solutions Blog
channel.description: Articles by John M Pogue on brand voice, AI adoption, automation, and capturing founder knowledge.

item.title: The One Piece of Gear Every New Creator Needs
item.dc:creator: John M Pogue
item.description: Before lights, microphones or editing apps, get a selfie stick that stands up as a tripod. Here is why it is the first thing I recommend to every client, and the exact one I tell them to buy.

item.title: What Should a Small Business Automate First?
item.dc:creator: John M Pogue
item.description: The first thing to automate is the task you repeat most often with the least judgment. Here is how to find it, why most businesses pick wrong, and a short method for deciding before you buy any software.

item.title: What Is Brand Voice AI?
item.dc:creator: John M Pogue
item.description: Brand Voice AI is an AI-assisted business operating system that captures a company's knowledge, voice, and standards so people and AI tools can create consistent work. Here is what it organizes, how it works, and who it is for.

item.title: How Do You Capture the Knowledge Inside a Founder's Head?
item.dc:creator: John M Pogue
item.description: Founder knowledge gets captured one conversation at a time, not in a single brain-dump session. Here is the interview method, the categories that matter, and why most documentation efforts fail before they start.

item.title: AI Has a New Name in Washington. Laughable or Not, Learn It.
item.dc:creator: John M Pogue
item.description: Washington now calls AI "super intelligence" and has a new Super Intelligence Force to match. What changed, who is in charge, and what small business owners should do about it.

item.title: Why I Named My AI Assistant Ms MoneyPenny
item.dc:creator: John M Pogue
item.description: What a land tech in an oil and gas office taught John M Pogue about the job an AI assistant should do: organize, draft, guard the calendar, and never send without a yes.

item.title: A Starship Traded Its Library for a Ride Home
item.dc:creator: John M Pogue
item.description: A 1995 Star Trek: Voyager episode explains why your stories are the one thing AI cannot produce when anyone can publish a thousand posts a day.

item.title: The Builders Asked for Brakes. The Government Gave Three Answers.
item.dc:creator: John M Pogue
item.description: AI companies asked to slow down. The government gave three answers at once. A Navy surgical count, film ratings, and the ESRB show what real oversight needs.

item.title: AI's "Wild West" Phase Needs a Regulator, Not a Waiver
item.dc:creator: John M Pogue
item.description: AI labs want an antitrust waiver to coordinate on safety. Lessons from debt collection and Sarbanes-Oxley point to an independent public referee instead.

item.title: Siri AI Ships Monday.
item.dc:creator: John M Pogue
item.description: Apple is paying Google to power the new Siri while building its own replacement. The Motorola ROKR shows how this partnership may end, and what small businesses can learn.

item.title: Your best customer already bought.
item.dc:creator: John M Pogue
item.description: Your past customers are your most valuable asset. Three ways a small business can sell them the next thing: the natural next purchase, a maintenance plan, and an introduction.

item.title: We Already Accepted the Machine. We Just Forgot We Did.
item.dc:creator: John M Pogue
item.description: In 1713 a boy rigged a steam engine to run its own valves. The same lesson applies to AI: automate the repetition and keep human judgment where it belongs.

item.title: AI Won't Take Your Job, But It Will Change Who Keeps It!
item.dc:creator: John M Pogue
item.description: The professionals who keep their jobs will direct, challenge, evaluate, and multiply AI output. A human and AI workflow for starting strong and finishing strong.

item.title: What's Your Bottleneck? Can AI Be the Solution?
item.dc:creator: John M Pogue
item.description: Adding AI does not remove a bottleneck. It can help you reach it faster. Where AI work slows down before, during, and after, and how to open the flow.

item.title: Afraid AI Will Take Your Job? Here's How to Become Harder to Replace
item.dc:creator: John M Pogue
item.description: How to become harder to replace with AI: open big by defining the problem, let AI do the heavy lifting, and close big with human judgment and accountability.

item.title: AI Marketing Is Not a Funnel Anymore. It Is a Business Operating System.
item.dc:creator: John M Pogue
item.description: Customers do not fall through a funnel. Marketing in the AI era needs continuity across research, brand, offers, content, and approval: a business operating system.

item.title: Tell Me Your Origin Story
item.dc:creator: John M Pogue
item.description: Marvel made superheroes human by showing their struggles. Your business has an origin story too, and telling it is how customers come to root for you.

item.title: Rebel Without a Claude: Stop Sounding Like Everyone Else's AI
item.dc:creator: John M Pogue
item.description: AI is making entrepreneurs sound alike. The fix is giving AI more of you: your stories, opinions, humor, and values, so it amplifies the identity you already have.

item.title: What Roger Corman Taught Me About Learning AI
item.dc:creator: John M Pogue
item.description: Three lessons from filmmaker Roger Corman that apply to learning AI: do the rough things first, plan but be ready to change, and open big and close big.

item.title: Don't Tell Me It Can't Be Done: Rethinking the LinkedIn Profile Ring
item.dc:creator: John M Pogue
item.description: LinkedIn only offers an #OpenToWork ring. How John M Pogue turned that limitation into a custom profile badge, a branding workflow, and a Custom GPT.

item.title: How I Lost 3.5 Years of ChatGPT History in One App Update
item.dc:creator: John M Pogue
item.description: One ChatGPT app update wiped three and a half years of organized projects. Why you should export your AI history every 90 days, and the backup guide to do it.

item.title: Why I Won't Miss the AI Revolution
item.dc:creator: John M Pogue
item.description: John M Pogue watched the internet and smartphone revolutions from the sidelines. Why he is prepared for the AI revolution, and why this time he is in the game.

item.title: Why Isn't America a Perfect 100? A Veteran's Curiosity About Freedom Rankings
item.dc:creator: John M Pogue
item.description: A veteran looks at why Freedom House scores the United States 81 out of 100, how freedom indexes define freedom, and what a homegrown scorecard might weigh.

item.title: The Future of Marketing Isn't Advertising. It's Shareable Experiences
item.dc:creator: John M Pogue
item.description: People rarely share ads. They share experiences. How businesses design photo-worthy moments that turn customers into brand ambassadors and earned media.

item.title: Why Credit Cards Are a Terrible "Emergency Fund"
item.dc:creator: John M Pogue
item.description: Available credit is not savings. Card companies can cut limits or close accounts when you need them most. The Credit Avenger case for a real cash reserve.

item.title: What I'd Do With a $2,000 Tariff Refund (Credit Avenger Style)
item.dc:creator: John M Pogue
item.description: The Credit Avenger plan for a $2,000 windfall: shore up the emergency fund, hit the debt snowball, kill a monthly payment, and invest in skills that pay.
